top_cited_works.title: Perfect selective metamaterial solar absorbers
top_cited_works.abstract: In this work, we numerically investigate the radiative properties of metamaterial nanostructures made of two-dimensional tungsten gratings on a thin dielectric spacer and an opaque tungsten film from UV to mid-infrared region as potential selective solar absorbers. The metamaterial absorber with single-sized tungsten patches exhibits high absorptance in the visible and near-infrared region due to several mechanisms such as surface plasmon polaritons, magnetic polaritons, and intrinsic bandgap absorption of tungsten. Geometric effects on the resonance wavelengths and the absorptance spectra are studied, and the physical mechanisms are elucidated in detail. The absorptance could be further enhanced in a broader spectral range with double-sized metamaterial absorbers. The total solar absorptance of the optimized metamaterial absorbers at normal incidence could be more than 88%, while the total emittance is less than 3% at 100°C, resulting in total photon-to-heat conversion efficiency of 86% without any optical concentration. top_cited_works.title: Coherent thermal emission by excitation of magnetic polaritons between periodic strips and a metallic film
top_cited_works.abstract: The present paper theoretically demonstrates coherent thermal emission in the infrared region by exciting magnetic polaritons between metallic gratings and an opaque metallic film, separated by a dielectric spacer. The coupling of the metallic strips and the film induces a magnetic response that is characterized by a negative permeability and positive permittivity. On the other hand, the metallic film intrinsically exhibits a negative permittivity and positive permeability in the near infrared. This artificial structure is equivalent to a pair of single-negative materials. By exciting surface magnetic polaritons, large emissivity peaks can be achieved at the resonance frequencies and are almost independent of the emission angle. The resonance frequency of the magnetic response can be predicted by an analogy to an inductor and capacitor circuit. The proposed structure can be easily constructed using micro/nanofabrication.

recent_works.title: A Study on the Integration of Teaching on Borrowing Costs and Financing Costs in International Trade Enterprises Under the Guidance of Ideological and Political Education in the Curriculum
recent_works.abstract: The in-depth advancement of ideological and political education in courses requires the organic integration of value-oriented guidance and professional knowledge at the theoretical level. This paper uses borrowing costs and the financing costs of international trade enterprises as knowledge carriers, incorporating the theory of incomplete markets from finance, the information economics theory from accounting, and the theory of externalities from international trade to construct an interdisciplinary analytical framework of “financing behavior—accounting recognition—economic consequences.” On this basis, the paper proposes an integration pathway for ideological and political education that is endogenous to the theoretical logic of the discipline, providing a theoretical foundation for finance and economics courses to achieve the unity of knowledge transmission and value cultivation.

recent_works.title: A Supply-Chain Assessment of Water Resource Allocation in China’s National Water Network and Water-Diversion Projects
recent_works.abstract: China’s national water network (NWN) aims to address water scarcity and uneven water distribution. However, existing studies on water-diversion projects (WDPs), primarily at the basin and provincial levels, often oversimplify benefit calculations by ignoring the complex topology of water-transfer projects and their interactions with inter-regional supply-chain networks. In this article, we collect detailed data on 76 completed WDPs and 11 WDPs under construction in China as of 2022. Using a multiagent complex network model coupled with data for water resources, water use, and the NWN, we simulate losses from water scarcity before and after the implementation of the NWN and various WDPs at different times and under different water resource conditions, considering the reduction in losses from water scarcity as a supply-chain benefit. We find that, after integrating the NWN with inter-city supply chains in China, regions with severe water scarcity and large amounts of diverted water, such as Shanghai, Lanzhou, Zhengzhou, Taiyuan, and Karamay, experience high benefits.
